sources.location: mqpar.xml (deposited MaxQuant 1.6.17.0 parameters, read) and RAW header range reads

claims.evidence: RAW header range-read of all 21 E* files shows Q Exactive; tune file 190514_nEASY_tune, method DDA 30 samples per day_15cm column. PRIDE lists only "Q Exactive"; paper Methods say QExactive HF, which matches the EH series only, so the deposit is split by instrument.
all 21 RAW files of this series claimed once; the other series is in the sibling SDRF; proteinGroups.txt and mqpar.xml are not RAW runs
RAW header scan-event text "nce: 25" and Fragmentation_HCD method element; Orbitrap HCD instrument
RAW headers, "nce: 25" in all 21 files of the series
Paper Methods: data-dependent mode; method names DDA
mqpar.xml enzymes=Trypsin/P, 2 missed cleavages; paper/PRIDE: trypsin, 1 ug overnight; PRIDE protocol: trypsin without proline restriction

claims.value: Carbamidomethyl (C) fixed; Oxidation (M) and Acetyl (Protein N-term) variable
claims.evidence: mqpar.xml fixedModifications / variableModifications; PRIDE data processing protocol agrees
Paper Methods: 10 mM DTT, 20 mM iodoacetamide
PRIDE organism; paper: human donor NK cells and human NK lines
All seven EV groups (primary NK cells, NK-92, KHYG-1) derive from NK cells per PRIDE description and paper
Experiment names 1-21 from mqpar.xml (each experiment pairs one E* and one EH* RAW file, so sibling SDRFs use identical source names); no deposited sample names
No mapping of experiments to triplicate groups; single value used only because source names are unique, not a claim of replicate identity

limitations: Which of the 21 experiments is primary NK / NK-92 / KHYG-1, and which is IL-15, IL-12/15/18 or anti-CD16 stimulated, is not recorded in any deposited file (mqpar.xml and proteinGroups.txt use numeric experiment names 1-21 only; RAW headers carry no sample names). The paper describes 7 groups x triplicates but not the run order. Therefore cell line, cellosaurus, treatment, organism part, disease, age, sex are not in the SDRF (or are `not available`) and there is no factor value. The cell-lines template was not declared because primary cells and cell lines cannot be assigned per row (cell line column has no reserved word).

characteristics[biological replicate] is 1 for every row as a placeholder because the triplicate grouping is undecodable; do not read it as replicate identity. Distinct experiments are distinguished by source name.

The paper states Q Exactive HF for the analysis, but RAW headers show the E* series was acquired on a Q Exactive (NCE 25) and EH* on a Q Exactive HF (NCE 28); the deposit is split into -QE and -HF SDRFs. The pairing of E* and EH* files as the same sample is inferred only from shared MaxQuant experiment names 1-21 in mqpar.xml (one combined search), not from a deposited mapping.

Sample is EVs isolated by precipitation (Total Exosome Isolation kit) from culture supernatants; no enrichment/material-type column was added because the contract has no honest single value across rows.
Both series were searched together in one MaxQuant run; tolerances and modifications are identical for both SDRFs. Fragment tolerance 20 ppm is the mqpar FTMS default for the Orbitrap analyzer.
Age, sex, ancestry and individual are `not available`: donors were anonymous healthy buffy-coat donors without per-sample data; cell lines are not assigned. Developmental stage omitted (optional).

SANDBOX ONLY (independent review FAIL): run-to-sample mapping is undecodable (mqpar.xml experiments 'experiment 1-21' appear in both series, proteinGroups columns are numbered only, RAW headers carry no sample names, paper supplements are figures), so cell line (primary NK / NK-92 / KHYG-1) and treatment (IL-15, IL-12/15/18, anti-CD16) are missing and biological replicate = 1 is a placeholder that contradicts the triplicate design (the ms-proteomics/human templates reject 'not available' for it). Precursor tolerance: mqpar.xml 4.5 ppm vs PRIDE text 6 ppm. Instrument split confirmed from all 42 RAW headers (E* = Q Exactive NCE 25, EH* = Q Exactive HF NCE 28).
